newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour says no U-turn on tobacco sponsorship.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour says no U-turn on tobacco sponsorship.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour party denied on Thursday that it had reversed its previous policy by promising to outlaw tobacco sponsorhip as well as advertising.

Campaign, an advertising industry magazine, said a speech by Labour health spokesman Kevin Barron last month pledging support for the European Union's proposed directive on tobacco advertising -- which would also outlaw sponsorship -- apparently marked a U-turn.
But Barron said this was incorrect. "We've always been in favour of the banning of tobacco advertising and promotion," he told Reuters.
Campaign said the thrust of Barron's speech contradicted comments a month earlier by Labour member of parliament Kate Hoey. But Barron said Hoey was not voicing party policy.
"That's not the way the (Labour) health team sees it at all," he said.

Speaking to a health forum in Strasbourg on October 23, Barron said a Labour government would favour prompt action to counter other forms of promotion that tobacco firms would try to devise once the proposed EU directive is passed and implemented.

"These attempts by tobacco companies to subvert our efforts as legislators to control their activities are likely to continue," Barron said. "These new forms of promotion will be the next battleground."
He added: "We must be ready to respond quickly and effectively to the challenge and we must be ready to stop these attempts at enticing young people to smoke."
